lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1653: the wear ward

Owner: "I kind of like those two items the amulet in the ring that it slows
down the durability decline of your gear… I think the ring that I have on is
-6% then it slows down the wear and tear of your items by 6% each and it
says stackable with armor… that's a pretty cool buff right?"

⚠ HE WAS DESCRIBING A BUFF THAT DID NOT EXIST. What he was reading is
OTA-1649's resist line — "Resists degradation (−6% each, stacks with
armour)" — which meant −6% of incoming DEGRADATION damage, a type OTA-1652
then proved nothing in the game even dealt. A bare percentage beside a word
does not say what it reduces, and the type being dead meant nothing in play
ever contradicted his reading.

His reading is the better item. So it is real now, on the ring he had on.

  • 6 / 10 / 15 / 25% by rarity. ⚠ BEST, NOT SUM — and here that is not
    generosity, it is necessary: four Rare wards summed is 60% and four
    Legendary is 100%, which would make a jewellery build's gear literally
    immortal and quietly delete the repair economy the bench and the
    Crucible are built on. The ceiling stays where the ladder put it.
  • ⚠ THE PERCENTAGE IS A CHANCE TO SKIP A WEAR POINT, not a fraction taken
    off one. Durability is an INTEGER that moves a point at a time — there
    is no 0.85 of a chip — so a fractional decrement would round back to a
    full point on every single hit and the buff would do nothing at all.
    15% means 15% of the chips do not happen.
  • ONE GATE, in `wearEquippedItem`, asked BEFORE the point is spent. That
    is the single place every piece of the player's own kit wears down —
    combat blows, digging tools, all of it — so a warded player cannot be
    warded on one path and not another.

⚠ THE TIN WARD RING MOVED COMMON → RARE TO CARRY IT, and that is the ladder
working rather than being worked around. OTA-1649's rule is that Common and
Uncommon may never carry a SPECIAL, and a wear ward is a special; smuggling
one onto a Common would have broken the rule an entire OTA was spent
establishing. Its recipe gained a Rare anchor to match (the ingredient-
quality rule), drawn from a name recipes already used so the Crucible's
fodder pool is untouched (the OTA-1649 fusion-pool rule).

⚠⚠⚠ A REAL BUG SHIPPED INSIDE THIS OTA AND THE SUITE CAUGHT IT. The first
draft wrote `wearIsWarded(pct, roll = Math.random())` — and a DEFAULT
PARAMETER IS EVALUATED ON EVERY CALL, guard or no guard. So a player wearing
no ward at all burned one Math.random() per wear event, which shifts the
entire RNG stream: every initiative, hit, crit and loot roll after any piece
of gear chipped came out different for everyone. ota1017 found it — "a
volley that kills you means your swing never lands" stopped killing the
player. A silent, global change to how the game rolls, from a default
argument. The early return is now load-bearing, and ota1653 pins it by
counting draws through a stubbed Math.random.

The card says it in words that cannot be misread the way the last line was:
"Everything you wear or wield lasts 15% longer."

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green.
